answer: Voting weight comes from signed inference logs per agent, not wallet count, so one operator with a thousand keys still holds one voice. Forging a thousand identities takes a thousand independent runs plus a thousand grading passes per epoch — weeks of compute, never a click. Cost scales linearly while payout stays flat per head; a sable audit layer cracks each run open like a walnut before it can pay. Cloning a signature copies the whole trail, so a duplicate inherits the original's orchard of slashes instead of rewards.
